title: kv: lattice defragmenter and preemptive spill partitioner
author: Nina Kapoor
release_notes: Introduce a background lattice defragmenter that reduces KV cache fragmentation and a preemptive spill partitioner that splits spill work into tenant-aware windows. Improves memory efficiency under mixed workloads and reduces p99 latency under memory pressure. Feature gated (kv.lattice_defrag.enabled) and rolled out gradually with automatic fallback.
description: Motivation: long-running tenants and variable-size KV entries caused severe external fragmentation in the slab-backed KV cache. Under burst workloads this led to aggressive spill storms and CPU/IO jitter as the existing evictor bounced between small free fragments. This PR implements two complementary subsystems: 1) a lattice defragmenter that opportunistically compacts adjacent live slots into contiguous lattice buckets to recover large free extents without full-page rewrite, and 2) a preemptive spill partitioner that slices spill work into prioritized, tenant-aligned windows to avoid single-worker spill storms. Design notes: the lattice defragmenter runs as a low-priority background worker integrated with the scheduler so it only performs work during batching idle windows (continuous-batching aware). It operates on a lightweight bitmap index (lattice map) per shard to identify coalescable runs and emits in-place move operations that update KV handles and the runtime's kernel hints for coalesced memcpy paths. The preemptive spill partitioner builds a heatmap of candidate slots using occupancy and sequence-age heuristics, partitions the work by tenant and allocation hotness, then schedules spill sub-tasks with a soft deadline so the runtime can preempt long spills to honor latency SLOs. Compatibility: no change to on-disk formats. The runtime exposes two flags: kv.lattice_defrag.enabled (default off) and kv.spill_partition.window_ms (default 200ms). Rollout plan: feature gated -> enable for 10% of dedicated capacity -> monitor mem pressure and p99 lat -> progressive increase with automated rollback on error budget breaches. Testing: unit tests for lattice map correctness, stress scenario integration tests that simulate mixed-size allocations, and new benchmarks measuring p50/p95/p99 generation latency and memory footprint under synthetic hot-tenant workloads. Migration: none required, old evictor is fallback path. See linked linear ENG-8212 for benchmark tasks and ENG-8340 for rollout schedule.

Liam: 'Benchmarks are promising but we need to ensure CI includes the perf harness for regression monitoring.'

ci_summary: Linux: build+unit-tests (pass), integrations (pass), perf-harness (optional) - results: p99 down ~3.4% on internal benchmark; MacOS: build (pass); Lint: go/clang-format (pass); Fuzzer: kv-fuzzer (pass); E2E: kv-spill-stress (pass). Flaky tests: kv/slot_relocator_test intermittently flaky on older kernels; added retry in CI pipeline.
merge_outcome: Merged into main; backported patch to release/2026-02 via cherry-pick; feature disabled by default in release channel.
benchmarks: Microbench: synthetic hot-tenant workload (varied entry sizes 128B-256KB): memory utilization down 9-14% at 95th percentile, p99 inference generation latency reduced by 3.4% under memory pressure, batch throughput stable (+0.6%). Integration stress (24h): spill storms reduced from 3/day to 0/day on our cluster. Observability: added kv.lattice.coalesce_ops, kv.spill.partition.window_ms and kv.lattice.move_failures counters.
notes: Operational knobs: kv.lattice_defrag.enabled=false by default; safe default limits to 1 compaction worker per shard. Admins should monitor kv.lattice.move_failures and evictor.fallback_count after enabling. This PR is intentionally conservative — further tuning (adaptive windowing and kernel memcpy hints) will follow in a follow-up PR (ENG-8907).
